The same map under several classifications

Source: R/honest-maps.R
classify_compare.Rd

Small multiples of one choropleth, drawn once per classification method, plus the break table and the count of countries in each class. The point is that the choice is consequential and usually unexamined: Brewer & Pickle (2002) found quantiles among the best methods for general choropleth reading and natural breaks (Jenks) below 70% as accurate, which is the reverse of the common GIS default.

Usage

classify_compare(
  data,
  value,
  methods = c("quantile", "jenks", "equal", "pretty"),
  n = 5,
  ncol = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

data

A map-ready frame (polygon or sf).

value

The value column (unquoted).

methods

Classification styles to compare. Any of "quantile", "jenks", "equal", "pretty" and "sd". "jenks" needs the optional classInt; without it, it falls back to quantile breaks with a warning.

n

Number of classes (default 5).

ncol

Number of facet columns.

...

Passed to world_map().

Value

A faceted ggplot object, with the per-method break and class-count table attached as the "countryatlas_classification" attribute (and readable with map_provenance()).

References

Brewer, C. A. & Pickle, L. (2002). Evaluation of methods for classifying epidemiological data on choropleth maps in series. Annals of the Association of American Geographers 92(4), 662-681. doi:10.1111/1467-8306.00310

See also

world_map(), map_provenance()

Examples

# \donttest{
snap <- countryatlas::world_snapshot$countries
if (requireNamespace("maps", quietly = TRUE)) {
  cmp <- attach_geometry(snap, geometry = "polygon") |>
    classify_compare(gdp_per_capita)
  attr(cmp, "countryatlas_classification")
}
